title: Domain Architecture
purpose: Transform the source-grounded domain understanding established in Domain Analysis into a governed architecture of domain boundaries, responsibilities, language, rules, state, decisions, data ownership, services, events, authority, integrations, and lifecycle change. Domain Architecture defines how domain meaning is partitioned and protected across the system and organization.
why_it_matters: Domain inconsistency is one of the most expensive forms of architectural debt because it spreads silently. A term can carry one meaning in a user journey, another in an API, another in a database, another in finance, and another in a model prompt. One service may treat an event as a fact while another treats it as a request. A workflow may encode an informal workaround as policy.
applies_when: The system spans multiple business, operational, scientific, legal, technical, organizational, or jurisdictional contexts.
Terms are overloaded, disputed, translated, or used differently by users, operators, systems, regulators, or data sources.
does_not_apply_when: A small isolated change uses stable, current, authoritative domain definitions within one existing bounded context and changes no meaning, ownership, rule, state, event, interface, authority, jurisdiction, or lifecycle behavior.
The work is user research about lived experience rather than domain structure; findings may inform but do not themselves establish domain authority.
prerequisites: Section 016 Domain Analysis and relevant Research, Business Analysis, Stakeholder Management, User Research, Requirements Engineering, Systems Engineering, Enterprise Architecture, Solution Architecture, and Systems Architecture outputs.
A legitimate human domain decision owner and identified authorities for definitions, rules, policy, data, decisions, exceptions, and jurisdiction.
Current authoritative sources, domain experts, operational evidence, systems, schemas, APIs, events, workflows, records, incidents, and known exceptions.
required_inputs: Authorized domain question, scope, intended use, decision owner, model owners, affected parties, environments, jurisdictions, and lifecycle horizon.

Domain Analysis outputs: canonical terms, actors, responsibilities, authority, concepts, entities, value objects, events, states, rules, invariants, exceptions, decisions, processes, information, boundaries, dependencies, and unresolved disputes.

Requirements and architecture outputs defining required capabilities, journeys, system elements, interfaces, data, policy, security, privacy, safety, reliability, accessibility, and evidence obligations.
human_authority: Authoritative humans and institutions retain responsibility for legitimate domain meaning, policy, law, values, exceptions, accountability, and decision rights. - Confirm domain scope, subdomain boundaries, bounded contexts, model owners, canonical language, invariants, exceptions, and source hierarchy. - Decide which differences are legitimate context-specific models and which are defects requiring convergence.
ai_boundary: AI may extract, compare, classify, model, map, translate, test, and document domain evidence within an explicit assignment. It may not invent domain truth, policy, legal meaning, authority, exception, consensus, source of truth, or final bounded-context decision. - Preserve source identity, owner, date, version, jurisdiction, effective period, applicability, and confidence for every material statement.
evidence_requirements: Evidence may include authoritative laws, regulations, contracts, standards, policy, procedures, manuals, forms, domain-expert review, user and operator research, records, transactions, schemas, APIs, events, code, workflows, incident history, audit findings, support cases, data lineage, examples, counterexamples, and observed state transitions.

Every material domain claim must identify its source, owner, version, jurisdiction, effective period, context, method, limitations, and relationship to the claim. Current software behavior, database design, majority usage, vendor terminology, AI output, or a single expert statement is not automatically authoritative.
failure_anti_patterns: One universal model forced across contexts with genuinely different responsibilities.
Database schema, class hierarchy, API shape, event payload, or prompt treated as the domain itself.
Same term used with different meanings without context or translation.
recovery: When the domain architecture is contradicted, disputed, or invalidated:
Identify the exact term, context, rule, state, event, source, owner, jurisdiction, effective date, interface, or decision affected.
Preserve the prior model, conflicting evidence, dissent, examples, incidents, and supersession history.
completion: Domain Architecture is DRAFT-complete only when:
Scope, contexts, jurisdictions, authority, owners, sources, lifecycle, and intended consumers are explicit.
Subdomains and bounded contexts have documented responsibilities, language, models, state, rules, data, services, events, and ownership.
source_gaps: Primary supplied source basis:
Thirsty's Standard v3 provides truthful scope, source inspection, evidence before claims, bounded work, independent verification, hostile review, continuity, and no fake completion.
learning_objectives: Recognize when the section is materially applicable.
Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.
Assign bounded roles without converting expertise into authority.
Determine what evidence/state is sufficient for the next transition and when to defer/suspend/request evidence.

title: Business Architecture
purpose: Define the governed structure of how an enterprise or bounded organization creates, delivers, sustains, governs, changes, and retires value. Business Architecture connects mission and strategy to stakeholders, value propositions, outcomes, value streams, capabilities, organizations, roles, decisions, policies, information, products, services, resources, measures, risks, controls, investments, and transition work.
why_it_matters: Strategy fails when it cannot be translated into an operating structure. Organizations may fund projects without knowing which enduring capability they improve. Teams may optimize local output while damaging an end-to-end value stream. Technology may automate an undocumented workaround or conceal a broken decision boundary.
applies_when: Mission, business, product, portfolio, program, project, or transformation strategy must be translated into an operating structure.
The enterprise needs to understand how value is created across organizational, product, service, process, information, technology, partner, or jurisdiction boundaries.
does_not_apply_when: A narrowly bounded change has no effect on value propositions, value streams, capabilities, operating model, decision rights, policy, organization, information, products, services, partners, measures, risk, controls, or lifecycle obligations, and current architecture evidence proves that conclusion.

The work is a temporary exploratory exercise that makes no claim of organizational approval, implementation, adoption, benefit, or operating readiness. The exercise must still state its boundary and limitations.
prerequisites: Sections 001-018 provide research, foresight, strategy, product, portfolio, program, project, market, stakeholder, user, domain, feasibility, and risk context.
Section 019 provides controlled requirements and acceptance boundaries.
Section 020 provides the system-of-interest and lifecycle engineering context where business operation depends on systems or enabling systems.
required_inputs: Authorized business question, objective, scope, exclusions, decision owner, and decision horizon.
Mission, business strategy, product strategy, portfolio priorities, program and project commitments.
Stakeholder and affected-party maps, user research, market research, competitive intelligence, and partner or supplier context.
human_authority: The authorized human owner remains responsible for: - Defining and approving mission, values, strategic outcomes, enterprise boundary, affected-party obligations, and acceptable tradeoffs. - Establishing legitimate decision owners and confirming the authority of participating executives, managers, domain experts, operators, employees, contractors, partners, and reviewers.
ai_boundary: AI may: - Retrieve, classify, compare, and summarize authorized source material. - Build current-state inventories, capability maps, value-stream models, decision maps, operating-model views, dependency graphs, traceability matrices, and option analyses.
evidence_requirements: Evidence may include mission and strategy records, owner decisions, governance documents, organization records, role definitions, policies, contracts, laws, regulations, budgets, portfolio data, product and service records, customer and user research, stakeholder evidence, operational observation, process records, transaction records, system telemetry, incident history, support cases, audits, risk assessments, control tests, workforce evidence, training records, supplier evidence, financial records, and benefit measurement.

Each material claim must identify source identity, version, environment, jurisdiction, effective date, method, scope, owner, limitations, and relationship to the claim. A policy does not prove operational behavior. A software feature does not prove business capability. A project completion record does not prove adoption or benefit. A metric does not prove value unless its definition, data lineage, incentives, and validity are known. An AI-generated map is not evidence of the organization.
failure_anti_patterns: Organization chart presented as Business Architecture.
Process inventory, application map, or project portfolio presented as a complete operating model.
Capability names derived from current systems, departments, vendors, or initiatives without stable outcome definitions.
recovery: When Business Architecture is blocked, contradicted, or invalidated:
Identify the exact claim, model element, decision, source, or dependency affected.

Classify the issue as authority, source identity, scope, objective, stakeholder, domain, capability, value stream, decision right, information, policy, measure, evidence, feasibility, risk, implementation, adoption, or transition failure.
completion: Business Architecture is complete for its declared scope only when:
Scope, authority, sources, current state, target state, transition state, assumptions, unknowns, and exclusions are explicit.

Mission, strategy, stakeholder outcomes, value propositions, value streams, capabilities, decisions, processes, information, products, services, systems, resources, controls, measures, investments, and lifecycle obligations are traceable.
source_gaps: Source basis:
Thirsty's Standard v3 supplies truthful status, evidence-before-claims, minimum effective change, verification, hostile review, continuity, recovery, and no-fake-completion discipline.
learning_objectives: Recognize when the section is materially applicable.
Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.
Assign bounded roles without converting expertise into authority.
Determine what evidence/state is sufficient for the next transition and when to defer/suspend/request evidence.

title: Capability Architecture
purpose: Define the governed architecture of the enduring abilities required to produce authorized outcomes. Capability Architecture identifies what an enterprise, system, product, service, organization, human-AI team, or ecosystem must be able to do, independent of the temporary projects, departments, applications, vendors, models, or processes used to realize that ability.
why_it_matters: Enterprises often organize change around projects, products, systems, or departments because those objects are visible and funded. The enduring ability to achieve an outcome can remain unclear. A project can finish while the required capability is unavailable, unauthorised, poorly integrated, unsupported, inaccessible, or fragile.
applies_when: Strategy, Business Architecture, Enterprise Architecture, product strategy, portfolio, or transformation work requires a stable view of enduring abilities.
Investments, programs, projects, products, services, systems, platforms, teams, suppliers, or AI initiatives must be compared against common outcome requirements.
does_not_apply_when: A bounded change neither creates, modifies, degrades, transfers, duplicates, depends on, or retires a capability, and current evidence supports that conclusion.
The work is exploratory and makes no claim that a capability exists, is authorized, is operational, or can be sustained. Hypotheses must remain labeled.
prerequisites: Sections 001-018 provide research, strategy, portfolio, program, project, market, stakeholder, user, domain, feasibility, and risk context.
Section 019 provides requirements, acceptance criteria, and traceability.
Section 020 provides system, enabling-system, lifecycle, verification, and validation context.
required_inputs: Authorized capability question, scope, enterprise or system boundary, exclusions, decision owner, horizon, and lifecycle state.
Mission, business strategy, product strategy, portfolio priorities, value propositions, outcomes, value streams, and operating-model decisions.
Stakeholder, affected-party, customer, user, employee, operator, partner, supplier, and ecosystem evidence.
human_authority: The authorized human owner remains responsible for: - Approving capability scope, definitions, outcomes, owners, priority, target levels, investment, and lifecycle decisions. - Determining which outcomes, obligations, rights, harms, and tradeoffs matter. - Assigning legitimate capability ownership and ensuring owners have appropriate authority, resources, information, and accountability.
ai_boundary: AI may: - Extract candidate capabilities from authorized strategy, value streams, requirements, operations, products, services, systems, and evidence. - Normalize labels, detect duplicates, map dependencies, compare realizations, trace gaps, and maintain catalogs. - Analyze capability options, scenarios, capacity, bottlenecks, concentration, resilience, transition, and evidence coverage.
evidence_requirements: Evidence may include strategy and architecture records, owner decisions, value-stream observations, process and function records, organization and role data, workforce and competency evidence, product and service performance, system telemetry, capacity and demand data, incidents, support records, continuity exercises, control tests, audits, financial evidence, supplier and contract records, user research, accessibility testing, security and privacy assessments, safety evidence, operational demonstrations, recovery tests, and benefit measurement.

Every capability claim must bind to exact scope, outcome, owner, realization, environment, demand, authority, time, method, evidence, limitations, and lifecycle state. The following are insufficient alone: a capability label, a documented process, a trained employee, a software feature, an installed system, a model benchmark, a vendor promise, a successful demo, a completed project, or a passing unit test.
failure_anti_patterns: Capability map copied from an organization chart, application portfolio, process hierarchy, vendor taxonomy, or project list.
Capability names that describe current tools, departments, or initiatives rather than enduring outcomes.
Capability declared present because a feature, employee, system, model, or provider exists.
recovery: When Capability Architecture is blocked or invalidated:
Identify the exact capability, definition, owner, realization, dependency, measure, evidence, or decision affected.

Classify the issue as scope, authority, terminology, outcome, realization, dependency, demand, capacity, quality, integration, resilience, support, accessibility, control, evidence, effectiveness, transition, or retirement failure.
completion: Capability Architecture is complete for its declared scope only when:
Scope, authority, source hierarchy, current state, target state, transition state, assumptions, unknowns, and exclusions are explicit.
Capability definitions are stable, outcome-based, non-duplicative, and sufficiently independent of current realization.
source_gaps: Source basis:
Thirsty's Standard v3 supplies truthful completion, evidence-before-claims, current-state inspection, verification, hostile review, continuity, recovery, and bounded reporting.
learning_objectives: Recognize when the section is materially applicable.
Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.
Assign bounded roles without converting expertise into authority.
Determine what evidence/state is sufficient for the next transition and when to defer/suspend/request evidence.

title: Process Architecture
purpose: Define the governed structure of how work, decisions, controls, information, evidence, exceptions, and recovery move through a bounded organization, system, service, product, or socio-technical capability. Process Architecture translates approved outcomes, capabilities, requirements, domain rules, operating concepts, and functional obligations into an intentional network of processes.
why_it_matters: Capabilities and systems do not produce outcomes by existing alone. People and machines act through sequences of work, decision points, information exchanges, controls, waits, handoffs, and recovery paths. A process that appears simple in a diagram may conceal unowned decisions, inaccessible steps, undocumented manual work, circular approval, weak evidence, or a recovery path that depends on the failed activity.
applies_when: A capability, value stream, product, service, system, organization, or human-AI workflow requires multiple activities, actors, decisions, handoffs, states, controls, or lifecycle stages.
Work crosses organizational, system, domain, supplier, partner, jurisdictional, physical, or data boundaries.
does_not_apply_when: The work is a bounded observation, text correction, or reversible change with no material effect on process sequence, decision rights, participants, controls, evidence, user journey, operating mode, or lifecycle state.
An approved and current process architecture already covers the exact scope, version, environment, population, variant, and change, and impact analysis shows no material process effect.
prerequisites: Sections 001-018 provide objective, strategy, stakeholder, user, domain, feasibility, and risk context.
Section 019 provides the requirements baseline, acceptance boundaries, mandatory constraints, variants, and traceability obligations.
Section 020 provides system, operational-concept, lifecycle, allocation, interface, verification, validation, transition, and recovery context.
required_inputs: Authorized process question, objective, scope, exclusions, decision owner, population, environment, jurisdiction, and lifecycle horizon.
Mission, strategy, value propositions, value streams, capabilities, products, services, operating-model decisions, and affected-party outcomes.
Requirements, acceptance criteria, risk treatments, feasibility conditions, domain rules, invariants, policies, contracts, standards, and architecture constraints.
human_authority: The authorized human owner retains authority over process purpose, protected outcomes, values, affected-party obligations, policy interpretation, decision rights, staffing or resource commitments, acceptable risk, exceptions, external commitments, automation boundaries, and final acceptance. - Confirm the process objective, scope, boundaries, non-goals, affected parties, environments, variants, and lifecycle stages.
ai_boundary: AI may inspect authorized process records, compare current and target flows, identify missing steps and handoffs, propose models, detect duplicate or conflicting activities, generate traceability, analyze queues and dependencies, draft evidence requests, simulate scenarios, and document decisions within an explicit assignment.
evidence_requirements: Every current-state process claim must identify the process, scope, version or observation period, environment, population, method, source, actor, evidence identity, and limitation.
A policy, procedure, diagram, interview, ticket, log, or system trace proves only the bounded claim it can support; none automatically proves effective or adopted operation.
failure_anti_patterns: Treating a process diagram as an implemented or effective process.
Defining the process around the preferred software, team, vendor, or current organization instead of the outcome and affected journey.
Confusing a capability, function, task, procedure, policy, workflow configuration, or organization chart with a process architecture.
recovery: Quarantine the affected process claim, definition, variant, approval, evidence, or execution state while preserving the last trusted version.

Identify whether the issue concerns objective, boundary, terminology, ownership, authority, participant, activity, decision, control, data, interface, evidence, performance, accessibility, security, safety, resilience, recovery, or lifecycle state.
Downgrade the affected status to the truthful state and prevent unsupported readiness, compliance, effectiveness, or outcome claims.
completion: Process Architecture is complete for its declared scope only when:
Objective, outcome, scope, boundary, owner, authority, population, environments, variants, non-goals, and lifecycle stages are explicit.
Process meaning is distinguished from capability, function, activity, task, procedure, policy, organization, system, and implementation.
source_gaps: Source basis:

Thirsty's Standard v3 supplies the posture of truthful scope, current-state inspection, explicit unknowns, evidence before claims, independent verification, hostile review, continuity, recovery, and no fabricated completion.
learning_objectives: Recognize when the section is materially applicable.
Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.
Assign bounded roles without converting expertise into authority.
Determine what evidence/state is sufficient for the next transition and when to defer/suspend/request evidence.

title: Functional Architecture
purpose: Define the governed structure of what a system, service, product, organization, human, AI agent, device, or enabling element must do to produce authorized outcomes under declared conditions. Functional Architecture decomposes approved requirements, operational concepts, process obligations, capabilities, domain rules, and system behavior into coherent functions and subfunctions.
why_it_matters: Requirements state what is authorized and required; process models state how work is coordinated in context. Functional Architecture makes the required behavior explicit enough to allocate, design, implement, test, verify, operate, recover, and retire.
applies_when: A system, service, product, organization, device, process, model, agent, or capability contains interacting behaviors, transformations, controls, decisions, or interfaces.
Requirements must be decomposed and allocated across people, functions, systems, components, services, devices, external providers, or lifecycle activities.
does_not_apply_when: The work is a bounded observation, documentation correction, or reversible change with no material effect on required behavior, functional allocation, interface, control, state, evidence, user journey, or lifecycle obligation.

A current approved functional architecture covers the exact objective, requirements baseline, version, environment, operating mode, interfaces, and change, and impact analysis confirms no material functional effect.
prerequisites: Sections 001-018 provide objective, strategy, stakeholder, user, domain, feasibility, and risk context.
Section 019 provides the controlled requirements baseline, acceptance criteria, verification methods, variants, mandatory constraints, and change obligations.
Section 020 provides system context, operational concept, functional analysis, allocations, elements, interfaces, lifecycle, verification, validation, transition, and recovery context.
required_inputs: Authorized functional question, objective, scope, exclusions, owner, environments, operating modes, user and operator populations, and lifecycle horizon.
Approved requirements baseline, acceptance criteria, verification methods, criticality, variants, constraints, risk treatments, feasibility conditions, and open findings.
System context, operational concept, mission threads, process architecture, capability model, domain model, business and enterprise architecture.
human_authority: The authorized human owner retains authority over objectives, required outcomes, values, mandatory constraints, system boundary, functional criticality, acceptance, risk, safety, privacy, accessibility, security, resource commitments, autonomy, and irreversible allocation or deployment decisions.
ai_boundary: AI may inspect requirements and architecture, identify candidate functions, normalize terminology, compare decompositions, generate behavior models, propose allocations, analyze dependencies, draft functional contracts, produce test ideas, simulate bounded scenarios, and identify evidence gaps within its assignment.
evidence_requirements: Every functional claim must identify subject, function identity, version, scope, environment, operating mode, conditions, method, evidence source, timeframe, actor, and limitations.
A requirement proves an obligation exists; a functional model proves how the obligation is represented; neither alone proves implementation or runtime behavior.
failure_anti_patterns: Treating a function list, component diagram, API list, prompt, feature list, benchmark, prototype, or simulation as proof of functional behavior.
Deriving functions from the current implementation and then calling them requirements or architecture without authorized analysis.
Decomposing too little to expose ownership, interfaces, controls, states, failure, evidence, or verification.
recovery: Quarantine the affected function, allocation, contract, baseline, evidence, approval, or readiness claim while preserving the last trusted state.

Classify the issue as objective, requirement, domain meaning, process, decomposition, actor, authority, input, output, state, contract, allocation, control, quality, evidence, implementation, interface, failure, recovery, or lifecycle defect.
Downgrade the affected functional state to `UNKNOWN`, `PROPOSED`, `BLOCKED`, `NOT VERIFIED`, `FAILED`, or another truthful state.
completion: Functional Architecture is complete for its declared scope only when:
Objective, outcomes, requirements baseline, scope, system boundary, environments, operating modes, affected parties, authority, non-goals, and lifecycle stages are explicit.
Function meaning is distinguished from capability, process, activity, task, procedure, policy, component, service, interface, implementation, and observed behavior.
source_gaps: Source basis:

Thirsty's Standard v3 supplies truthful scope, current-state inspection, explicit unknowns, evidence before claims, independent verification, hostile review, continuity, recovery, and no fabricated completion.
learning_objectives: Recognize when the section is materially applicable.
Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.
Assign bounded roles without converting expertise into authority.
Determine what evidence/state is sufficient for the next transition and when to defer/suspend/request evidence.

title: Operational Architecture
purpose: Define how an approved capability, product, service, system, or organization is put into use and kept within its intended authority, performance, safety, security, support, continuity, and lifecycle boundaries. Operational Architecture connects process and functional design to real operating modes.
why_it_matters: A system can be architecturally coherent and still fail because no one knows who operates it, what happens outside the happy path, how authority expires, or how the service is restored after a dependency fails. Operational Architecture makes the lived operating environment explicit before implementation or launch is treated as success. It also prevents operations from becoming an unowned afterthought.
applies_when: A product, service, system, capability, facility, process, or organization will be used by people or automated actors over time.
Operation requires roles, schedules, procedures, monitoring, support, resources, approvals, controls, or service commitments.
does_not_apply_when: The artifact is a purely explanatory model with no claim of readiness, deployment, operation, support, or service effect.
The change is bounded, reversible, and has no material effect on operating roles, procedures, controls, dependencies, evidence, support, recovery, or lifecycle state.
prerequisites: Sections 019-020 provide requirements, operational concept, lifecycle, allocation, verification, validation, transition, and recovery context.
Sections 021-028 provide enterprise, solution, systems, domain, business, capability, process, and functional boundaries.
Current-state evidence identifies actual operators, environments, dependencies, support burden, incidents, capacity, and recovery behavior.
required_inputs: Approved objective, scope, service or capability outcomes, users, affected parties, environments, jurisdictions, modes, and lifecycle horizon.
Process and functional models, system elements, information and data obligations, interfaces, controls, requirements, risks, and acceptance criteria.
Deployment topology, schedules, staffing, skills, facilities, vendors, contracts, credentials, tools, budgets, support channels, and communication paths.
human_authority: The accountable human owner retains authority over service purpose, operating risk, commitments, staffing, resource allocation, policy interpretation, exceptions, release or launch readiness, incident severity, external communication, recovery tradeoffs, and final acceptance. - Confirm operating scope, modes, populations, environments, non-goals, and service boundaries.
ai_boundary: AI may inspect operational records, correlate signals, draft runbooks, classify alerts, propose schedules, simulate capacity or failure, summarize incidents, identify drift, and recommend bounded actions within explicit delegation. AI must label observation, inference, forecast, recommendation, action, and verified result separately; preserve source and time boundaries; expose uncertainty and missing telemetry;
evidence_requirements: Each operational claim identifies the exact service, version, environment, mode, population, time, method, actor, source, and limitation.
A runbook, dashboard, drill, simulation, or readiness review does not by itself prove effective operation.
failure_anti_patterns: Treating deployment, uptime, a green dashboard, or a completed runbook as proof of operational success.
Leaving operators, support, suppliers, facilities, staffing, training, or communication unmodeled.
Designing only the normal path and omitting degraded, emergency, offline, maintenance, recovery, and retirement modes.
recovery: On uncertainty, loss of authority, unsafe condition, major drift, or material evidence failure, stop or narrow affected actions and preserve state and evidence.
Identify the exact blocker, safe work that may continue, authority needed, evidence required, recovery owner, and review deadline.
Use approved fallback, isolation, failover, manual operation, rollback, restore, provider substitution, or service reduction paths.
completion: Scope, owners, authorities, modes, dependencies, services, procedures, controls, evidence, measures, and lifecycle states are explicit.
Normal, boundary, degraded, emergency, maintenance, recovery, migration, and retirement paths are addressed or justified as not applicable.
Readiness, support, observability, security, privacy, safety, accessibility, continuity, and human-control conditions are traceable.
source_gaps: This draft is based on the Canonical Section Contract, shared governance files, Sections 001-028, the Owner Cockpit Requirements, the Status and Evidence Lexicon, and the Remaining-Section Integration Roadmap.
The supplied Codex does not provide a single ratified operational standard for every sector, service level, safety regime, staffing model, jurisdiction, or technology environment.
learning_objectives: Recognize when the section is materially applicable.
Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.
Assign bounded roles without converting expertise into authority.
Determine what evidence/state is sufficient for the next transition and when to defer/suspend/request evidence.

title: Information Architecture
purpose: Define how information is named, organized, related, described, discovered, presented, exchanged, governed, and retired so that people and systems can understand and use it within authorized context. Information Architecture concerns meaning and access across journeys, processes, products, services, applications, records, interfaces, and operating environments.
why_it_matters: People and systems cannot make reliable decisions from information that is ambiguous, stale, inaccessible, misclassified, or impossible to find. Poor information structure creates duplicate records, hidden authority, unsafe defaults, privacy leakage, inconsistent terminology, and user journeys that cannot be completed. Information Architecture makes meaning and context deliberate.
applies_when: People or systems must find, interpret, compare, exchange, update, publish, retain, or retire information.
Multiple domains, products, services, organizations, languages, jurisdictions, roles, or applications use related information.
does_not_apply_when: The work has no material effect on meaning, labels, context, discoverability, access, representation, provenance, retention, user journey, or lifecycle.
An approved information architecture covers the exact domain, audience, version, environment, and change, with impact analysis showing no material effect.
prerequisites: Sections 016, 019, and 020 provide domain meaning, requirements, system boundaries, information obligations, verification, validation, and lifecycle context.
Sections 021-029 provide enterprise, solution, systems, domain, business, capability, process, functional, and operational context.
Data ownership, privacy, security, records, accessibility, localization, and legal constraints are known or marked unresolved.
required_inputs: Objectives, audiences, affected parties, user and operator journeys, domains, contexts, languages, jurisdictions, environments, and lifecycle stages.
Domain terms, business rules, requirements, process and functional models, data inventories, records schedules, policies, contracts, and standards.
Current content, taxonomies, catalogs, schemas, metadata, search behavior, navigation, interfaces, logs, support records, user research, and accessibility evidence.
human_authority: The accountable human owner retains authority over domain meaning, definitions, classification, audience obligations, rights, publication, access, privacy, retention, deletion, correction, exceptions, and acceptance. - Confirm information scope, audiences, purposes, contexts, boundaries, terminology, and non-goals.
ai_boundary: AI may inventory information, compare vocabularies, propose taxonomies, identify duplicates, map concepts, analyze journeys, draft metadata, test findability, and recommend context or presentation within explicit authority. AI must preserve source identity, provenance, version, audience, context, uncertainty, and permission; distinguish source information from inference and generation;
evidence_requirements: Each information claim identifies source, owner, version, scope, audience, context, date, method, permission, and limitation.
A label, taxonomy, search result, citation, diagram, or user statement proves only its bounded claim and not universal comprehension or correctness.
failure_anti_patterns: Treating discoverability, fluency, search rank, citation, or visual polish as proof of truth or comprehension.
Mixing source, interpretation, inference, recommendation, and generation without labels or provenance.
Creating a universal taxonomy that ignores domain, audience, language, jurisdiction, accessibility, or lifecycle context.
recovery: On semantic conflict, provenance loss, permission uncertainty, stale source, harmful disclosure, or inaccessible path, restrict affected use and preserve the prior record.
Name the blocker, safe uses that continue, owner, authority, evidence, review date, and affected audiences.
Use approved quarantine, source substitution, prior version, manual review, restricted presentation, rollback, withdrawal, or correction paths.
completion: Scope, audiences, contexts, definitions, structures, sources, lineage, ownership, permissions, accessibility, lifecycle, and evidence are explicit.
Ambiguous, conflicting, generated, stale, restricted, denied, and recovery conditions are addressed or justified.
Users and owners can inspect, correct, restrict, withdraw, and recover information within authority.
source_gaps: This draft uses the Canonical Section Contract, shared governance files, Sections 001-029, Owner Cockpit Requirements, Status and Evidence Lexicon, and the Remaining-Section Integration Roadmap.
No universal supplied vocabulary, taxonomy, information classification, records schedule, accessibility standard, retention rule, or sector-specific disclosure regime applies to every future system.
learning_objectives: Recognize when the section is materially applicable.
Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.
Assign bounded roles without converting expertise into authority.
Determine what evidence/state is sufficient for the next transition and when to defer/suspend/request evidence.

title: Data Architecture
purpose: Define the governed structure and lifecycle of data: what data exists, what it means, where it comes from, how it moves and changes, who owns it, how it is protected and qualified, and when it is retained, archived, migrated, deleted, or destroyed.
why_it_matters: Data is often treated as inert material when it is actually a source of decisions, obligations, identity, automation, records, and harm. Wrong lineage, stale values, incompatible schemas, missing consent, weak deletion, or unowned quality can make an otherwise functional system untrustworthy. Data Architecture makes data behavior explicit across its full life rather than at one storage boundary.
applies_when: A system creates, receives, stores, transforms, exchanges, analyzes, publishes, generates, retains, archives, migrates, or deletes data.
Data influences identity, rights, safety, privacy, security, finance, compliance, operations, models, decisions, or user experience.
does_not_apply_when: The change has no material effect on data meaning, source, schema, flow, quality, access, lifecycle, evidence, or user or system outcomes.
An approved data architecture covers the exact scope, data classes, environment, version, population, and change, with impact analysis showing no material effect.
prerequisites: Sections 016, 019, 020, and 030 provide domain, requirements, systems, information, lifecycle, evidence, and context obligations.
Sections 021-029 provide architecture, capability, process, functional, and operational ownership and boundaries.
Privacy, security, records, legal, quality, accessibility, resilience, and AI governance constraints are known or explicitly open.
required_inputs: Objectives, domains, entities, data subjects, users, operators, jurisdictions, environments, sensitivity, purposes, and lifecycle.
Business rules, requirements, information structures, processes, functional contracts, application boundaries, interfaces, events, and controls.
Source inventories, schemas, metadata, lineage, data dictionaries, catalogs, records schedules, access policies, quality results, incidents, and migration history.
human_authority: The accountable human owner retains authority over purpose, collection, classification, consent or other lawful basis, sharing, quality thresholds, access, retention, correction, migration, deletion, risk, and acceptance. - Confirm data scope, purpose, subjects, domains, jurisdictions, environments, sensitivity, and non-goals.
ai_boundary: AI may inventory data, compare schemas, identify lineage gaps, propose models or quality rules, analyze distributions, draft mappings, detect anomalies, and generate migration or test ideas within authorized data access. title: Governance Architecture
purpose: Define how authority, policy, delegation, decision rights, evidence, oversight, exceptions, accountability, change, and lifecycle are structured and enforced across the system.
why_it_matters: Governance is the boundary between capability and permission. Without explicit authority and immutable decisions, policy becomes informal, exceptions become invisible, and an AI or operator can turn a recommendation into an unreviewed commitment.
applies_when: A system makes decisions, grants authority, changes policy, invokes tools, manages records, affects rights, or creates external consequence.
Multiple owners, policies, jurisdictions, suppliers, agents, or lifecycle stages require coordination and precedence.
does_not_apply_when: No decision right, policy, authority, delegation, exception, evidence, or lifecycle governance effect changes.
An approved governance baseline covers exact scope and change with no material impact.

human_authority: Authorized humans define policy, precedence, values, decision rights, risk appetite, quorum, exceptions, overrides, acceptance, and compensation. They approve, deny, revoke, investigate, appeal, supersede, and retire governance decisions. No AI recommendation creates authority.
ai_boundary: AI may classify requests, retrieve policy, identify conflicts, draft evaluations, summarize evidence, and recommend decisions. It must bind claims to policy and evaluation evidence, preserve uncertainty, and default to escalation or denial. It must not approve mutations, invent policy, bypass quorum, or replace immutable decisions.
evidence_requirements: Each decision identifies intent, subject, action, resource, policy, evaluation, capability, authority, trace, evidence, outcome, and expiry.
A prompt, local check, approval message, or successful mutation without binding is not governance evidence.
failure_anti_patterns: Local-only policy checks, unsigned or mutable decisions, missing trace, incomplete binding, or silent overrides.
Treating approval, model confidence, capability possession, or successful execution as sufficient governance.
Destructive rollback, hidden audit mutation, quorum bypass, authority inheritance, or default-allow conflict resolution.
recovery: On binding failure, policy conflict, revoked capability, audit loss, or partial mutation, deny or halt and preserve records.
Identify safe read-only work, decision owner, evidence, affected resources, and appeal or reconsideration path.
Recover only through a new authorized decision and compensation linked to the prior immutable decision.
completion: Authority, policy, evaluation, binding, decision, quorum, audit, trace, artifact, conflict, appeal, compensation, and lifecycle are explicit.
Default-deny, immutable decision, append-only audit, replay, and non-destructive recovery are verified.

title: Safety Architecture
purpose: Define hazards, harms, safety constraints, protective functions, human oversight, operating limits, fail-safe behavior, evidence, and lifecycle controls for systems that can affect people, property, environment, or public safety.
why_it_matters: Safety failure can be physical, social, environmental, or cumulative. A passing nominal test does not establish safe behavior under uncertainty, misuse, degraded sensing, human fatigue, model drift, or recovery.
applies_when: A system can affect health, bodily safety, property, environment, public services, rights, or high-consequence decisions.

why_it_matters: Reliability is contextual and time-dependent. A system that works once or has high uptime can still fail too often, recover too slowly, or degrade users through hidden maintenance and common-cause dependencies.

prerequisites: Purpose, audience research, world and domain context, character and content rules, medium, localization, sensitivity, accessibility, rights, and acceptance authority.
required_inputs: Purpose, audience research, world and domain context, character and content rules, medium, localization, sensitivity, accessibility, rights, and acceptance authority.
human_authority: Humans approve theme, representation, audience, content boundaries, rights, sensitivity, and acceptance. They resolve value conflicts and retain publication and correction authority.

evidence_requirements: Identify source, author, audience, medium, version, cultural context, review method, result, and limitation. Emotional response or continuity score is bounded evidence.

title: Content Design
purpose: Define content that helps a declared audience understand, decide, act, recover, and maintain an accurate mental model of a product, service, or system.
why_it_matters: Content is part of behavior and can create legal, safety, privacy, and trust consequences. Clear prose is not automatically accurate or inclusive.
applies_when: Applies to interface, help, instructional, transactional, error, notification, onboarding, support, and operational content.
does_not_apply_when: No material meaning, instruction, disclosure, action, accessibility, localization, or recovery effect; or an unchanged approved content baseline with impact recorded.
prerequisites: Information architecture, user research, requirements, domain terms, policies, product behavior, accessibility, localization, legal review, source evidence, and authority.
required_inputs: Information architecture, user research, requirements, domain terms, policies, product behavior, accessibility, localization, legal review, source evidence, and authority.
human_authority: Humans approve meaning, claims, audience, tone, disclosure, rights, safety, accessibility, and publication. They retain correction, withdrawal, and acceptance authority.
ai_boundary: AI may draft, transform, translate, and critique content. It must preserve source, context, uncertainty, and rights and must not invent facts, cite nonexistent sources, or publish consequential text.
evidence_requirements: Identify source, claim, audience, context, version, reviewer, method, result, and limitation. Readability or engagement is bounded evidence.
failure_anti_patterns: Invented claims; vague errors; manipulative consent; untranslated critical content; inaccessible tables; stale help; and content that promises behavior the system does not perform.
recovery: Withdraw or correct content, preserve prior evidence, notify affected users, provide human support, and retest behavior and locales before republishing.
completion: Audience, purpose, claims, sources, states, accessibility, evidence, tests, correction, recovery, open risks, and acceptance are explicit. Remain CONTENT-COMPLETE pending review and acceptance.

title: Content Strategy
purpose: Define the strategic purpose, portfolio, governance, investment, measurement, and lifecycle of content across audiences, channels, products, and services.
why_it_matters: Content strategy prevents fragmented publication, contradictory claims, inaccessible information, and unmanaged maintenance burden.
applies_when: Applies when content is a material product, service, operational, marketing, instructional, support, or records capability.
does_not_apply_when: No material content outcome, audience, channel, claim, governance, resource, or lifecycle effect; or an unchanged approved strategy with impact recorded.
prerequisites: Mission, product and service strategy, information architecture, research, content inventory, channel data, policies, legal, accessibility, localization, staffing, and decision authority.
required_inputs: Mission, product and service strategy, information architecture, research, content inventory, channel data, policies, legal, accessibility, localization, staffing, and decision authority.
human_authority: Humans set content purpose, priorities, claims, audiences, resources, risk, governance, and acceptance. They approve commitments and resolve conflicting stakeholder needs.
ai_boundary: AI may inventory content, synthesize evidence, and propose priorities. It must expose evidence quality and opportunity cost and must not set editorial policy or publish claims.
evidence_requirements: Identify source, audience, channel, period, method, result, uncertainty, and limitation. Traffic, reach, or engagement is bounded evidence.
failure_anti_patterns: Publishing without owners; optimizing volume; treating traffic as value; ignoring maintenance; contradictory channels; inaccessible archives; and no retirement path.
recovery: Pause unsupported publication, preserve decisions, correct or withdraw content, assign owners, commission research, and rebaseline affected channels.
completion: Mission, audiences, portfolio, governance, resources, evidence, measures, risks, recovery, open gaps, and acceptance authority are explicit. Remain CONTENT-COMPLETE pending review and acceptance.

title: Technical Writing
purpose: Define accurate, task-oriented technical documentation for building, using, operating, troubleshooting, securing, maintaining, and retiring a system.
why_it_matters: Technical documentation can become an operational control. Incorrect or stale instructions can cause outage, unsafe action, data loss, or unsupported commitments.
applies_when: Applies to developer, API, operator, administrator, user, support, installation, migration, security, and retirement documentation.
does_not_apply_when: No material instruction, configuration, API, task, safety, security, accessibility, or recovery effect; or an unchanged approved document with impact recorded.
prerequisites: Implementation and runtime evidence, requirements, interfaces, procedures, versions, users, accessibility, localization, security, support, records, and technical authority.
required_inputs: Implementation and runtime evidence, requirements, interfaces, procedures, versions, users, accessibility, localization, security, support, records, and technical authority.
human_authority: Humans approve technical truth, warnings, supported scope, risks, publication, and acceptance. Owners retain correction, withdrawal, and escalation authority.
ai_boundary: AI may draft, transform, index, and test documentation. It must preserve source, version, environment, commands, and uncertainty and must not invent behavior or claim execution it did not perform.
evidence_requirements: Identify source, artifact, version, environment, reader, method, test result, date, and limitation. A rendered page or grammar review proves bounded quality only.
failure_anti_patterns: Stale commands; invented flags; examples that leak secrets; missing prerequisites; no recovery; version ambiguity; inaccessible code blocks; and documentation treated as tested because it renders.
recovery: Withdraw unsafe guidance, preserve source and prior version, publish correction, notify affected users, and retest dependent procedures before restoring status.
completion: Reader, task, version, source, evidence, tests, warnings, recovery, lifecycle, open risks, and acceptance are explicit. Remain CONTENT-COMPLETE pending review and acceptance.

title: Copywriting
purpose: Define persuasive, clear, and responsible language for an approved audience, offer, identity, or action without misleading, coercing, or hiding material conditions.
why_it_matters: Copy can create commitments, shape consent, and influence vulnerable audiences. Persuasion must not substitute for truth, comprehension, or fair choice.
applies_when: Applies to marketing, product, campaign, transactional, onboarding, notification, fundraising, public, and brand copy.
does_not_apply_when: No material claim, offer, disclosure, consent, audience, accessibility, localization, or action effect; or an unchanged approved copy baseline with impact recorded.
prerequisites: Objective, audience research, offer, product behavior, substantiation, legal and policy constraints, brand, accessibility, localization, privacy, and approval authority.
required_inputs: Objective, audience research, offer, product behavior, substantiation, legal and policy constraints, brand, accessibility, localization, privacy, and approval authority.
human_authority: Humans approve claims, audience, fairness, disclosure, consent, rights, risk, publication, and acceptance. They retain correction, withdrawal, and complaint authority.
ai_boundary: AI may generate variants and analyze performance. It must preserve substantiation, audience context, and uncertainty and must not invent testimonials, scarcity, guarantees, or targeting rationale.
evidence_requirements: Identify claim, source, audience, channel, version, method, result, limitation, and reviewer. Conversion or engagement is bounded evidence.
failure_anti_patterns: Dark patterns; false urgency; hidden fees; fake social proof; inaccessible disclosures; unsubstantiated superiority; and optimizing conversion over informed choice.
recovery: Pause publication, correct or withdraw claims, notify affected audiences, preserve evidence, offer remedy where authorized, and retest before reuse.
completion: Audience, objective, claims, substantiation, disclosures, evidence, tests, recovery, risks, and acceptance are explicit. Remain CONTENT-COMPLETE pending review and acceptance.

title: Localization
purpose: Define adaptation of content, interaction, data, behavior, and support for a declared locale while preserving meaning, functionality, accessibility, legal fit, and cultural respect.
why_it_matters: Literal translation can break meaning, layout, dates, numbers, safety, humor, consent, or legal disclosure. Locale coverage is not cultural validity.
applies_when: Applies to products, services, content, interfaces, support, data, voice, games, documentation, and operations used across locales.
does_not_apply_when: No locale, translation, formatting, cultural, accessibility, legal, or audience effect; or an unchanged approved localization baseline with impact recorded.
prerequisites: Source content, locale requirements, terminology, translators, cultural research, legal and policy rules, format constraints, accessibility, testing, and authority.
required_inputs: Humans approve locale scope, meaning, cultural fit, legal disclosures, accessibility, publication, and acceptance. They resolve untranslatable or sensitive content.
human_authority: AI may translate or identify variants, but must preserve source, context, uncertainty, and human review. It must not invent cultural authority or publish high-consequence translation alone.
ai_boundary: AI may prepare locale-specific drafts, detect inconsistent terminology, flag truncation or cultural risk, and assemble traceable comparison and test evidence from approved source material. It must preserve source intent, locale scope, formatting rules, accessibility requirements, legal meaning, uncertainty, and reviewer attribution; distinguish translation from adaptation;
evidence_requirements: Identify source, locale, translator or model, context, version, method, result, uncertainty, and limitation. Back-translation or fluency is bounded evidence.
failure_anti_patterns: Machine translation without review; English fallback for critical content; truncated scripts; cultural stereotypes; wrong units; and treating fluency as correctness.
recovery: Use approved fallback, remove harmful translation, preserve source and review history, notify owners, commission qualified review, and retest affected locales.
completion: Locales, source, meaning, review, accessibility, evidence, tests, fallback, recovery, risks, and acceptance are explicit. Remain CONTENT-COMPLETE pending review and acceptance.

title: Internationalization
purpose: Define product and system foundations that allow locale, language, culture, legal, accessibility, and regional variation without unsafe rewrites or hidden assumptions.
why_it_matters: Internationalization failures surface late as broken layouts, incorrect calculations, exclusion, or legal error. Early variation modeling reduces systemic rework and hidden regional assumptions.
applies_when: Applies to products, platforms, data, content, APIs, services, operations, and systems expected to support more than one locale or cultural context.
does_not_apply_when: No locale, language, format, culture, legal, accessibility, or regional behavior effect; or an unchanged approved foundation with impact recorded.
prerequisites: Target locales, language and script requirements, data and format rules, content, architecture, legal, privacy, accessibility, testing, deployment, and authority.
required_inputs: Humans approve supported locales, defaults, regional obligations, data boundaries, accessibility, legal fit, tradeoffs, and acceptance.
human_authority: AI may identify hard-coded assumptions and generate locale tests. It must preserve evidence and uncertainty and must not select regional policy or infer cultural meaning without authority.
ai_boundary: AI may inspect code, content, schemas, and tests for locale assumptions; propose variation points; generate representative fixtures; and report unsupported scripts, formats, parsing paths, or fallback behavior. It must preserve locale and regional scope, data meaning, privacy boundaries, accessibility, precision, timezone, currency, and uncertainty, and must separate detection from implementation and acceptance.
evidence_requirements: Identify locale, platform, data, format, version, test method, result, uncertainty, and limitation. Passing one locale proves bounded support only.
failure_anti_patterns: Hard-coded strings; locale as decoration; incorrect numeric or date parsing; global defaults; untestable formatting; and falling back to a language that hides critical meaning.
recovery: Restrict unsupported locale, preserve data, use approved fallback, correct formatting, notify owners, and retest affected locales before expansion.
completion: Locale model, variation, data, formats, accessibility, tests, evidence, fallback, recovery, risks, and acceptance are explicit. Remain CONTENT-COMPLETE pending review and acceptance.
source_gaps: Based on the Canonical Section Contract and shared governance files. Actual locale matrix, supported scripts, regional data rules, legal obligations, and acceptance thresholds remain unresolved.

title: Accessibility Design
purpose: Define inclusive experiences, interfaces, content, environments, and controls that people with varied abilities can perceive, understand, operate, and recover from.
why_it_matters: Accessibility is an outcome and a rights concern, not a final visual check. Exclusion often occurs in error, recovery, timing, content, and support paths.
applies_when: Applies to products, services, content, physical or digital interfaces, devices, documents, environments, and owner or operator controls.
does_not_apply_when: No material access, task, content, control, assistive, timing, or recovery effect; or an unchanged approved accessibility baseline with impact recorded.
prerequisites: Users and disability research, requirements, interaction and content models, target technology, applicable standards, devices, assistive tools, privacy, and acceptance authority.
required_inputs: Humans approve inclusion goals, standards, risk, accommodations, exceptions, resources, and acceptance. They must include affected people and retain correction, appeal, and stop authority.
human_authority: AI may identify barriers and generate test ideas. It must not infer disability, claim accessibility from heuristics, or replace lived-experience review and qualified testing.
ai_boundary: AI may inspect interfaces, content, documents, and workflows for potential barriers; map findings to approved standards; propose equivalent alternatives; and generate bounded test cases for keyboard, assistive technology, sensory, cognitive, timing, and recovery paths.
evidence_requirements: Identify population, access mode, technology, standard, task, method, result, limitation, and date. Automated scans and conformance claims prove bounded coverage only.
failure_anti_patterns: Treating a scan as acceptance; inaccessible recovery; color-only meaning; inaccessible authentication; accommodations hidden; and claiming compliance without version, scope, or evidence.
recovery: Provide equivalent path or accommodation, preserve user progress, remediate and communicate barriers, record exceptions, and retest before removing restrictions.
completion: Population, tasks, standards, alternatives, evidence, tests, exceptions, recovery, risks, and acceptance authority are explicit. Remain CONTENT-COMPLETE pending review and acceptance.
source_gaps: Based on the Canonical Section Contract, shared governance files, and accessibility evidence conventions. Actual standards, populations, technologies, accommodations, jurisdiction, and acceptance thresholds remain unresolved.

title: Design Systems
purpose: Define reusable design tokens, components, patterns, content, behavior, accessibility, governance, and release controls that support coherent experiences without suppressing justified variation.
why_it_matters: Design systems reduce duplication but can spread a defect at scale. Reuse must preserve context, accessibility, behavior, and user outcomes.
applies_when: Applies to shared UI, interaction, content, visual, motion, voice, code, token, and service patterns.
does_not_apply_when: No shared component, token, pattern, accessibility, behavior, release, or consumer effect; or an unchanged approved system baseline with impact recorded.
prerequisites: UX and UI architecture, component consumers, requirements, accessibility, content, code, versioning, testing, contribution, support, and authority.
required_inputs: Humans own system purpose, standards, accessibility, versioning, exceptions, contribution, support, and acceptance. They decide when reuse harms context and retain deprecation authority.
human_authority: AI may inventory drift, generate variants, and suggest tokens or tests. It must preserve source and context and must not merge, release, or enforce patterns without governance.
ai_boundary: AI may inventory components, tokens, variants, consumers, drift, and test gaps; propose reusable patterns; and generate documentation, migration options, and bounded regression evidence from approved system sources.
evidence_requirements: Identify component, version, consumer, platform, state, test, method, result, and limitation. Component existence or snapshot coverage proves bounded reuse only.
failure_anti_patterns: One-size-fits-all components; hidden breaking changes; inaccessible defaults; token drift; documentation without code parity; and reuse prioritized over task outcome.
recovery: Quarantine defective component, preserve consumer versions, publish migration or fallback, notify owners, and retest all affected consumers before broad release.
completion: Scope, ownership, components, versions, accessibility, evidence, tests, migration, recovery, open risks, and acceptance are explicit. Remain CONTENT-COMPLETE pending review and acceptance.
source_gaps: Based on the Canonical Section Contract and shared governance files. Actual consumers, platforms, standards, component scope, contribution model, and acceptance thresholds remain unresolved.

title: Prototyping
purpose: Define the governed use of prototypes to learn about a proposed product, service, process, interaction, architecture, technology, or operating concept before treating it as an approved design or implementation. Prototyping creates bounded representations for inquiry.
why_it_matters: Prototypes make uncertainty visible while change is still relatively inexpensive. They expose misunderstanding, workflow gaps, technical constraints, accessibility barriers, unsafe assumptions, integration friction, and user burden that are easy to miss in prose or diagrams. They also create a recurring source of false confidence.
applies_when: A proposed outcome, requirement, interaction, workflow, service, architecture, component, integration, model, or operational concept contains material uncertainty.
Stakeholders need to compare alternatives, expose assumptions, or inspect a future state before committing to implementation.
does_not_apply_when: The work is a purely explanatory sketch with no claim beyond communication and no material change to requirements, decisions, user expectations, data, or authority.

An approved and current prototype or design evidence package answers the exact question for the same scope, population, environment, version, and decision, and impact analysis shows no material change.
prerequisites: Sections 001-020 provide objective, stakeholder, user, domain, feasibility, risk, requirements, systems, verification, validation, transition, and recovery context.

Sections 021-104 provide the applicable enterprise, solution, systems, domain, business, capability, process, functional, operational, information, data, application, user-experience, design, accessibility, and design-system boundaries.
The prototype owner, learning question, intended audience, decision authority, allowed environment, data boundary, and consequence limit are identified.
required_inputs: Authorized problem or opportunity statement, intended outcome, non-goals, scope, affected parties, population, environment, jurisdiction, and lifecycle horizon.
Requirements, user research, domain rules, process and functional models, architecture constraints, risks, acceptance criteria, and open decisions.
Prototype hypothesis, learning questions, alternatives, assumptions, success signals, disconfirming signals, fidelity level, and time limit.
human_authority: The authorized human owner retains authority over the prototype question, protected outcomes, participant treatment, risk tolerance, data and environment access, external commitments, interpretation of evidence, promotion, abandonment, and final decision. - Confirm the question, scope, fidelity, audience, non-goals, consequence boundary, and decision date.
ai_boundary: AI may help frame hypotheses, generate alternative concepts, create bounded mock data, draft prototype code or content, simulate scenarios, compare observations, identify missing states, and summarize evidence within authorized scope. AI must label generated, simulated, observed, measured, inferred, and human-supplied material separately;
evidence_requirements: Each claim identifies the prototype, version, question, scope, environment, population, method, date, actor, source, result, and limitation.
A mock-up, demo, successful execution, benchmark, simulation, interview, survey, or pilot proves only the bounded question it was designed to examine.
failure_anti_patterns: Treating a polished interface, clickable flow, technical spike, pilot, or demo as proof of product readiness or user value.
Testing only the happy path while hiding denial, error, accessibility, support, recovery, manual work, or operational cost.
Fabricating, selectively reporting, or averaging away negative feedback, dissent, failed runs, or affected-party burden.
recovery: On unsafe behavior, privacy or security exposure, misleading claims, participant harm, evidence loss, authority conflict, or scope drift, stop the session and preserve relevant evidence.
Identify the blocker, affected people, safe work that may continue, containment owner, authority, communication, and review condition.
Revoke credentials, isolate systems, delete or quarantine data, reset state, withdraw materials, notify affected parties, and obtain specialist review as required.
completion: The question, hypothesis, scope, fidelity, owner, authority, environment, controls, evidence method, and stop condition are explicit.
The artifact distinguishes real, simulated, generated, stubbed, manual, omitted, and observed behavior.
Relevant user, operator, accessibility, privacy, security, safety, operational, and recovery conditions are addressed or justified.
source_gaps: This draft uses the Canonical Section Contract, shared governance files, Sections 001-104, Owner Cockpit Requirements, Status and Evidence Lexicon, and the Remaining-Section Integration Roadmap.
No universal prototype fidelity scale, research protocol, participant incentive rule, statistical threshold, technology stack, or promotion gate applies to every future context.

title: User Validation
purpose: Define the governed process for determining whether a proposed or implemented product, service, system, process, interaction, content, or operating change supports the intended users and affected people under declared real or representative conditions. User Validation examines outcomes, not merely opinions or task completion.
why_it_matters: A system can meet its written requirements and still fail the people who must live with it. Users may be unable to discover a control, understand a status, complete a task, recover from an error, access content, challenge a decision, or trust what the system is claiming. People excluded from the study may carry the greatest burden.
applies_when: A change may affect user goals, comprehension, workflow, accessibility, safety, privacy, security, dignity, rights, trust, burden, or recovery.
A product, service, system, process, content, interaction, AI behavior, policy, or operating model is proposed for a defined population or context.
does_not_apply_when: The change has no material effect on user or affected-party outcomes, access, comprehension, burden, privacy, safety, security, accessibility, control, or recovery.
An approved validation package covers the exact population, context, version, outcome, and change, and impact analysis shows no material effect.
prerequisites: Sections 001-020 provide objectives, stakeholders, users, domain, feasibility, risk, requirements, systems, verification, validation, transition, and recovery context.

Sections 021-104 provide applicable architecture, process, functional, operational, information, data, application, human-computer interaction, experience, accessibility, content, and design-system boundaries.
The target population, affected non-users, intended outcome, decision authority, version, test environment, and consequence limits are explicit.
required_inputs: Authorized validation question, intended outcome, user jobs, affected parties, population, context, jurisdiction, environment, version, and lifecycle stage.
Requirements, acceptance criteria, prototypes or implementation, domain rules, process and functional models, architecture, risks, policies, and known constraints.
Participant segments, recruitment criteria, accessibility needs, language, devices, assistive technology, skills, support conditions, and exclusion risks.
human_authority: The authorized human owner retains authority over the outcome being validated, participant treatment, population definition, evidence sufficiency, risk acceptance, policy interpretation, design or release decision, and commitments made to users or affected people. - Confirm the validation question, intended outcome, population, context, version, non-goals, and decision boundary.
ai_boundary: AI may help identify user segments, draft tasks, generate accessible variants, summarize authorized sessions, code observations, compare patterns, identify missing outcomes, and propose follow-up research within the approved boundary. AI must preserve participant identity protections, consent or authorization, population, context, version, method, source, uncertainty, dissent, and limitations;
evidence_requirements: Each finding identifies question, population, context, version, method, task, date, source, observer or instrument, result, uncertainty, and limitation.
A quote, survey response, task success, completion time, benchmark, support ticket, rating, or session proves only its bounded claim.
failure_anti_patterns: Treating satisfaction, preference, a small positive sample, task completion, engagement, or internal approval as universal validation.
Recruiting only convenient or enthusiastic participants and describing the result as representative.
Leading participants, suppressing dissent, discarding non-completion, or averaging away material disparities.
recovery: On participant harm, privacy or security exposure, unsafe behavior, accessibility exclusion, invalid method, sample failure, evidence loss, or scope drift, stop the activity and protect affected people.
Identify the blocker, affected groups, containment owner, authority, communication, evidence preservation, and safe work that may continue.
Withdraw or correct misleading findings, notify affected participants when required, restrict records, revoke access, and obtain specialist review.
completion: Question, outcome, population, context, version, method, owner, authority, safeguards, criteria, and evidence limits are explicit.
Representative tasks and material user, affected-party, accessibility, safety, privacy, security, control, and recovery conditions are addressed or justified.
Findings include positive, negative, contradictory, missing, and unresolved evidence, with material differences preserved.
source_gaps: This draft uses the Canonical Section Contract, shared governance files, Sections 001-105, Owner Cockpit Requirements, Status and Evidence Lexicon, and the Remaining-Section Integration Roadmap.
No universal participant recruitment standard, sample-size threshold, research ethics regime, accessibility test method, outcome metric, or acceptance threshold applies to every future context.

Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.

title: Software Engineering
purpose: Define the disciplined creation, modification, verification, delivery, operation, maintenance, and retirement of software within approved requirements, architecture, authority, quality, security, privacy, safety, accessibility, and lifecycle boundaries. Software Engineering turns authorized intent into maintainable software artifacts and evidence.
why_it_matters: Software is executable authority. A small change can alter data, security, user rights, service continuity, safety, cost, or auditability. Engineering controls make intent, change, provenance, defects, and recovery visible across the full software lifecycle.
applies_when: Software is designed, coded, configured, generated, integrated, tested, released, operated, maintained, migrated, or retired.
A change affects behavior, interfaces, data, permissions, performance, reliability, accessibility, security, privacy, safety, or evidence.
does_not_apply_when: The work is a read-only inspection or explanatory note with no alteration to software, configuration, dependency, evidence, or lifecycle state.
An approved engineering baseline covers the exact artifact, version, environment, and change, and impact analysis finds no material effect.
prerequisites: Requirements, functional and operational architecture, security, privacy, safety, accessibility, reliability, and risk constraints are available or marked unresolved.
Source-control, build, dependency, artifact, environment, test, release, and incident ownership is assigned.
The target runtime, support horizon, licensing obligations, data boundary, and acceptance authority are known.
required_inputs: Approved requirements, interfaces, architecture, constraints, risks, acceptance criteria, and change request.
Source tree, build instructions, dependency manifests and locks, toolchain versions, environment definitions, and artifact locations.
Test strategy, quality thresholds, threat model, accessibility requirements, observability needs, release plan, support model, and recovery objectives.
human_authority: The accountable human owner approves scope, priorities, risk, quality thresholds, technology choices, exceptions, release readiness, support commitments, and retirement. Humans must review material design and code changes, approve security and privacy consequences, and accept only the exact version and evidence examined.
ai_boundary: AI may explain code, draft implementation, generate tests, identify defects, propose refactors, summarize changes, and analyze build or runtime evidence within an explicit assignment. It must identify generated or inferred content, preserve source context, expose uncertainty, and stop when requirements, authority, security, privacy, safety, or evidence are unclear.
specialist_expertise_cues_not_authority: Role selection is proportional to consequence
evidence_requirements: Each claim identifies artifact, version, environment, method, actor, date, result, limitations, and exact scope.
Build, test, review, scan, deployment, runtime, user, and operational evidence remain distinct.
failure_anti_patterns: Treating compilation, code coverage, a green pipeline, or deployment as proof of outcome.
Merging unreviewed generated code, floating dependencies, unverifiable binaries, or undocumented environment changes.
Hiding defects, accessibility failures, security findings, license conflicts, or operational burden.
recovery: Stop affected promotion on material uncertainty, failed controls, unsafe behavior, provenance loss, or invalid evidence. Preserve source, artifacts, logs, decisions, and user impact. Use approved isolation, rollback, restore, hotfix, substitution, or compensation; reassess requirements and reopen the baseline when assumptions or dependencies change.
completion: Scope, ownership, design, source, dependencies, build, review, tests, evidence, release, support, recovery, and retirement are explicit. Material findings are resolved, accepted by authorized humans, or recorded as blockers. This draft is not proof of implementation or production readiness.
source_gaps: Based on the Canonical Section Contract, shared governance files, Sections 019-032, Owner Cockpit Requirements, Status and Evidence Lexicon, and lifecycle conventions.

Sector-specific engineering standards, language policies, licensing rules, toolchain constraints, support commitments, and acceptance thresholds remain unresolved until supplied for the actual system.
