title: Policy
purpose: Create, approve, communicate, implement, monitor, interpret, review, and retire governing statements that direct behavior, authority, risk, rights, and controls.
why_it_matters: Policies can be ambiguous, contradictory, inaccessible, unenforced, or detached from actual work. A signed document is not proof that people understood it, systems implemented it, or exceptions were governed.
applies_when: Apply when a rule, standard, principle, commitment, restriction, or decision framework governs people, systems, data, products, operations, suppliers, or agents.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability when no governing behavior, authority, protected outcome, or control is affected and an approved exact baseline covers the scope.
prerequisites: Identify authority, affected parties, purpose, legal and regulatory sources, existing policies, processes, controls, enforcement, accessibility, communication, and review owner.
required_inputs: Objective, scope, authority, definitions, principles, requirements, exceptions, stakeholders, risks, evidence, implementation, communication, appeals, review cadence, and source conflicts.
human_authority: Policy owners draft and maintain policy; authorized humans approve, interpret material ambiguity, grant exceptions, resolve conflicts, communicate changes, and retire obsolete rules. Affected people must have a route to question, appeal, or report harm.
ai_boundary: AI may compare sources, identify contradictions, draft language, map policy to controls, and summarize feedback. It must preserve authority, source, version, scope, and uncertainty. It must not silently change meaning, create obligations, interpret law conclusively, approve, enforce, or hide dissent without human authority.
evidence_requirements: Identify policy, authority, version, scope, effective date, source, reviewer, control, implementation, communication, result, and limitation. Publication or acknowledgment proves neither comprehension nor operation.
failure_anti_patterns: Policy sprawl, contradictory rules, undefined terms, secret policy, inaccessible text, no owner, exceptions without expiry, and enforcement that differs from the approved policy.
recovery: Pause or narrow affected enforcement, preserve versions and decisions, notify owners, correct communication, remediate harm, and use the prior valid policy where authorized. Reopen on legal, operational, technological, user, or risk change.
completion: Purpose, authority, scope, sources, definitions, controls, exceptions, communication, evidence, review, appeal, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending authorized approval and owner acceptance.

title: Ethics
purpose: Make value conflicts, foreseeable harms, affected parties, power differences, duties, tradeoffs, and accountability explicit in decisions that are not settled by technical or legal analysis alone.
why_it_matters: A technically feasible or legally permitted action can still be harmful, unfair, exploitative, deceptive, or inconsistent with the human purpose. Ethics work must not become a decorative approval after the decision is already fixed.
applies_when: Apply when choices affect people, rights, dignity, safety, opportunity, privacy, communities, environment, future users, or power relationships, especially when automation or AI influences outcomes.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when the change has no affected person, value conflict, material externality, or consequential choice and an approved exact baseline supports it. Technical simplicity is not a sufficient reason.
prerequisites: Use user research, risk, privacy, safety, security, legal, accessibility, policy, impact, and governance evidence. Identify affected and absent voices, decision owner, escalation, and review authority.
required_inputs: Objective, options, stakeholders, affected non-users, values, constraints, benefits, harms, uncertainty, evidence, alternatives, power differences, safeguards, monitoring, and unresolved dissent.
human_authority: Humans identify values, listen to affected people, resolve moral tradeoffs, set unacceptable harm, approve safeguards, and accept or reject residual impact. No agent may transfer that responsibility to a score, majority, policy, or technical metric.
ai_boundary: AI may surface affected parties, compare options, identify value conflicts, summarize supplied perspectives, and challenge assumptions. It must not claim moral authority, manufacture consensus, erase dissent, infer values from proxy data, or decide human worth, rights, harm, or acceptable tradeoff without accountable human deliberation.
evidence_requirements: Identify claim, affected party, source, perspective, method, date, assumption, uncertainty, decision, safeguard, and limitation. A principle, survey, model output, or legal permission is not complete ethical evidence.
failure_anti_patterns: Ethics washing, token consultation, consensus theater, value substitution by metrics, absent affected parties, harm externalized to powerless people, and “legal means ethical” reasoning.
recovery: Pause or narrow harmful action, protect affected people, preserve evidence, seek missing perspectives, remedy where possible, and revisit the decision with accountable owners. Reopen on new harm, population, purpose, evidence, technology, or value change.
completion: Purpose, affected parties, values, options, harms, safeguards, authority, evidence, dissent, recourse, monitoring, limitations, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending independent challenge and owner acceptance.
source_gaps: Based on the Canonical Section Contract, shared governance, human-AI interaction requirements, and the integration roadmap. Exact ethical framework, affected communities, participation, authority, remedies, jurisdiction, and acceptance evidence remain unresolved.

title: Intellectual Property
purpose: Identify, protect, attribute, license, use, create, transfer, and retire intellectual-property interests and restrictions affecting the work.
why_it_matters: Ownership and permission can be unclear across employees, contractors, suppliers, open-source projects, generated material, data, and jurisdictions. A repository or citation is not proof of permission, ownership, originality, or compliant reuse.
applies_when: Apply when the work creates, uses, modifies, distributes, trains on, embeds, names, publishes, or derives value from potentially protected works, inventions, data, marks, or confidential material.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when qualified review confirms no protected or restricted material, contributor claim, license, confidentiality, publication, or transfer is affected.
prerequisites: Use Legal, Licensing, Records, Security, Privacy, Procurement, employment, supplier, and source-control baselines. Identify contributors, employers, licensors, repositories, jurisdictions, confidentiality, and approval authority.
required_inputs: Assets, authors, contributors, source and provenance, licenses, contracts, data, dependencies, marks, inventions, confidentiality, publication plan, notices, restrictions, and unresolved ownership questions.
human_authority: Owners and qualified counsel approve ownership, assignment, license, attribution, publication, disclosure, enforcement, and use of restricted material. Humans resolve contributor disputes and decide whether a source or generated artifact may be used.
ai_boundary: AI may inventory supplied sources, compare license text, track provenance, draft attribution and review questions, and identify possible conflicts. It must not assert originality, ownership, permission, authorship, or legal sufficiency; it must not ingest restricted material or publish, license, or disclose work without authorized human decision.
evidence_requirements: Identify asset, source, author, contributor, date, license or contract, jurisdiction, approval, version, method, result, and limitation. A URL, repository, generated output, or citation proves neither permission nor ownership.
failure_anti_patterns: Untracked copied code or data, license mixing, missing attribution, confidential material in public artifacts, authorship assumed from tool output, and publication before rights review.
recovery: Restrict distribution, preserve provenance and claim evidence, notify owners and counsel, replace or remove affected material, correct notices, and assess downstream copies. Reopen on new source, contributor, license, jurisdiction, publication, or claim information.
completion: Assets, sources, contributors, ownership, licenses, restrictions, approvals, notices, evidence, publication, recovery, limitations, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending qualified review and owner acceptance.

title: Licensing
purpose: Select, record, comply with, monitor, and retire licenses governing software, data, content, services, models, hardware, and other received or distributed material.
why_it_matters: Licenses create conditions on use, modification, distribution, attribution, disclosure, data, support, and termination. Package presence or a license file does not prove compatibility, notice delivery, or compliance in the shipped context.
applies_when: Apply when the work consumes, modifies, embeds, distributes, trains on, publishes, or operates licensed software, data, content, models, APIs, hardware, or services.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when no licensed or restricted asset, dependency, distribution, notice, renewal, or termination obligation is affected and an approved exact baseline supports it.
prerequisites: Use IP, Legal, Procurement, Security, Privacy, Supply Chain, Build, Release, Records, and Vendor baselines. Identify licensors, versions, transitive dependencies, recipients, jurisdictions, and approval authority.
required_inputs: Asset and dependency inventory, license text, version, source, licensor, rights, restrictions, notices, obligations, distribution model, consumers, contracts, renewals, exceptions, and evidence.
human_authority: Owners and counsel approve license selection, compatibility, distribution, attribution, disclosure, renewal, termination, exceptions, and risk. Humans resolve ambiguous or conflicting terms and approve shipped artifacts.
ai_boundary: AI may inventory dependencies, extract supplied license terms, compare obligations, draft notices and questions, and identify missing records. It must not interpret ambiguous terms conclusively, approve compatibility, remove notices, accept risk, or distribute material without qualified human authority.
evidence_requirements: Identify asset, version, source, licensor, license, contract, artifact, distribution, method, reviewer, result, and limitation. A package manager record or license filename proves only its captured metadata.
failure_anti_patterns: License assumed from package name, transitive dependency ignored, notices dropped, incompatible terms combined, expired entitlement, and distribution before approval.
recovery: Restrict affected artifact or distribution, preserve records, notify owners and counsel, replace or remediate material, correct notices, and assess downstream recipients. Reopen on dependency, license, contract, artifact, jurisdiction, or distribution change.

title: Records Management
purpose: Identify, classify, create, capture, protect, retain, retrieve, preserve, transfer, and dispose of records that provide evidence of obligations, decisions, rights, operations, or history.
why_it_matters: Records must remain usable and trustworthy for the period required, while unnecessary retention increases privacy, cost, and discovery risk. A backup, document, log, or database row is not automatically a record or an authoritative copy.
applies_when: Apply when information documents business, legal, regulatory, financial, safety, security, product, user, operational, or governance activity or must be preserved for accountability.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when no record, hold, retention, evidence, right, audit, or disposition obligation is affected and an approved exact baseline supports the conclusion.
prerequisites: Use Legal, Regulatory, Privacy, Security, Data, Evidence, Audit, Backup, Archive, and Deletion baselines. Identify jurisdictions, owners, record classes, authoritative systems, holds, retention authority, and disposal approval.
required_inputs: Record classes, sources, metadata, owners, business and legal value, retention, access, integrity, holds, jurisdictions, disposition, transfers, systems, evidence, and exceptions.
human_authority: Records owners and counsel approve classification, retention, hold, access, transfer, disposition, and exceptions. Humans resolve whether a record is authoritative, whether a hold applies, and whether destruction is lawful and safe.
ai_boundary: AI may classify authorized metadata, identify duplicates, draft inventories, summarize records, and propose retention or disposition queues. It must preserve provenance and not delete, alter, reclassify, disclose, or declare a record non-authoritative without explicit human authority and hold checks.
evidence_requirements: Identify record, source, class, authority, version, metadata, integrity, owner, hold, retention, access, method, time, result, and limitation. A backup or export proves only its capture and declared completeness.

why_it_matters: Change can break behavior outside the edited area through shared dependencies, data, configuration, timing, policy, or user journeys. A large suite can still miss the changed risk or hide flaky and obsolete cases.

title: Load Testing

why_it_matters: Expected load is not a single number. Arrival pattern, concurrency, data mix, cache state, dependency behavior, and duration determine whether a service remains useful or degrades.
applies_when: Apply when concurrent users, requests, jobs, devices, events, or transactions can affect capacity, latency, cost, or reliability.

evidence_requirements: Identify workload, rate, concurrency, duration, version, environment, data, dependency, metric, method, result, and limitation. One load profile proves only that profile.
failure_anti_patterns: Load against shared production without authority, generator bottleneck, unrealistic traffic, ignored dependency impact, throughput-only success, and load test that becomes an outage.

title: Stress Testing
purpose: Evaluate behavior beyond expected operating conditions and determine how the system degrades, protects people and data, recovers, and returns to service.
why_it_matters: Systems often fail in the transition between healthy and unavailable. Stress testing reveals queue collapse, retry storms, memory or resource exhaustion, unsafe fallback, data corruption, and recovery that was never exercised.
applies_when: Apply when overload, dependency loss, resource exhaustion, failure combination, extreme input, or environmental boundary can affect safety, continuity, integrity, or service.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when no adverse condition or recovery claim is material and an approved exact baseline covers the scope.
prerequisites: Use performance, load, reliability, resilience, safety, security, recovery, capacity, and operations baselines. Establish isolation, monitoring, stop, restore, and communication authority.
required_inputs: Stress scenario, limit, trigger, workload, environment, data, dependencies, safety constraints, expected degradation, recovery objective, instrumentation, and acceptance criteria.
human_authority: Owners approve adverse conditions, safety, data, production-like scope, stop, recovery, and residual risk. Operators control the exercise and can halt it immediately.
ai_boundary: AI may draft stress scenarios, analyze telemetry, and identify degradation patterns. It must not create unsafe conditions, continue after stop, alter recovery, or claim resilience from a simulation without human authority and evidence.
evidence_requirements: Identify condition, trigger, workload, version, environment, resource, time, method, result, user impact, recovery, and limitation. A successful recovery in one failure mode proves only that mode.
failure_anti_patterns: Stress without isolation, no stop path, destructive load, retry amplification, recovery not observed, data corruption ignored, and resilience claimed from uptime before failure.
recovery: Stop and stabilize, preserve evidence, restore or fail over under authority, protect users, communicate, and reassess residual risk. Reopen on architecture, workload, dependency, recovery, or safety change.
completion: Condition, safety, workload, degradation, recovery, evidence, owner, limits, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending qualified review and owner acceptance.

title: Scalability Testing
purpose: Determine whether a system can grow across users, data, traffic, devices, tenants, geography, workload, or time while preserving protected outcomes and acceptable cost.
why_it_matters: A system may handle more traffic but fail with data growth, tenant count, geographic spread, coordination, cost, or operator load. Linear extrapolation from a small test can hide thresholds and discontinuities.
applies_when: Apply when expected or strategic growth can affect performance, reliability, cost, privacy, security, data lifecycle, operations, or user experience.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when no growth dimension or scale-dependent outcome changes and an approved exact baseline covers the scope.

It must expose assumptions and uncertainty and must not promise scale, trigger capacity changes, or optimize cost at the expense of protected outcomes without human review.
evidence_requirements: Identify growth dimension, version, workload, data, environment, scale step, metric, cost, method, result, uncertainty, and limitation. Extrapolation must state its assumptions and validation boundary.
failure_anti_patterns: Linear extrapolation, traffic-only scaling, data and operator load ignored, cost surprise, shared tenant failure, autoscaling without guardrails, and growth commitments without evidence.

why_it_matters: Reliability is time and condition dependent. A short successful test can miss wear, memory growth, intermittent faults, retry amplification, operator error, dependency loss, or recovery that does not restore the intended outcome.

title: Resilience Testing

why_it_matters: Resilience is more than availability. A service may stay online while losing integrity, privacy, safety, user agency, or recoverability. Recovery plans without exercised authority and evidence are assumptions.
applies_when: Apply when disruption, dependency loss, resource failure, human absence, attack, environmental change, or organizational shock can affect essential outcomes.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when no protected outcome, dependency, continuity, recovery, or disruption claim is material and an approved exact baseline covers it.
prerequisites: Use operational, continuity, disaster recovery, reliability, safety, security, capacity, backup, restore, communication, staffing, and ownership baselines.

ai_boundary: AI may model dependencies, draft scenarios, analyze recovery evidence, and identify gaps. It must not declare resilience, trigger failover, change service mode, or suppress user and operator impact without delegated human authority.
evidence_requirements: Identify outcome, scenario, version, environment, dependency, authority, method, time, result, impact, recovery, and limitation. A failover drill proves only the exercised path and conditions.
failure_anti_patterns: Availability-only resilience, exercise without stop, dependency correlation ignored, recovery dependent on failed system, user impact hidden, and drill success treated as durable resilience.

title: Chaos Engineering
purpose: Learn how systems and organizations behave under controlled, hypothesis-driven disruption and use the evidence to improve resilience, detection, recovery, and human control.
why_it_matters: Resilience assumptions remain hidden until challenged. Uncontrolled chaos is simply an incident; controlled experiments require safety, observability, a meaningful hypothesis, and authority to stop.
applies_when: Apply when controlled disruption can safely answer a material resilience or operational question that ordinary testing cannot.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability when risk or authority cannot support a controlled experiment, a lower-risk test answers the question, or no material resilience uncertainty exists.
prerequisites: Define steady state, hypothesis, scope, blast radius, authorization, safety, abort, contacts, observability, rollback, recovery, communication, and incident conversion.
required_inputs: Hypothesis, protected outcome, target, version, dependency, disruption, limits, environment, telemetry, rollback, responders, data, and acceptance criteria.
human_authority: Experiment owners approve hypothesis, scope, risk, safety, stop, communication, and recovery. A controller can abort immediately; humans interpret learning and decide remediation.
ai_boundary: AI may draft hypotheses, dependency maps, experiment plans, and analysis. It must not initiate or escalate disruption, conceal impact, change targets, or declare steady state without explicit human authority and live supervision.
evidence_requirements: Identify experiment, hypothesis, target, version, disruption, environment, authority, time, observation, result, impact, recovery, and limitation. A successful experiment proves only its declared hypothesis and conditions.
failure_anti_patterns: Chaos without hypothesis, no abort, broad blast radius, missing telemetry, surprise to responders, experiment mistaken for incident, and learning without remediation.
recovery: Abort, stabilize, preserve evidence, recover, communicate, and convert to incident handling when necessary. Reassess hypothesis and safeguards before repeating. Reopen on system, dependency, threat, or operational change.
completion: Hypothesis, scope, safety, authority, evidence, result, impact, recovery, learning, remediation, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending independent review and owner acceptance.

why_it_matters: Automated checks find some structural issues but cannot establish actual comprehension, operability, dignity, or recovery. Inaccessible design can deny access even when the feature is technically functional.

title: Compliance Testing
purpose: Test whether declared controls and operating practices satisfy applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, policy, or standard-based criteria for their exact scope and period.
why_it_matters: Compliance is contextual and time-bound. A control can be designed but not operating, a certificate can be stale, and an automated check can miss the obligation's meaning or population.
applies_when: Apply when a claim of compliance, conformity, certification, attestation, contractual adherence, or regulatory control is required or material.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only after qualified review of authority, jurisdiction, entity, activity, period, and obligation, with the alternative evidence and reopening condition recorded.
prerequisites: Use legal, regulatory, policy, records, control, audit, privacy, security, quality, and evidence baselines. Define qualified reviewer, criteria, and attestation authority.
required_inputs: Authority, criteria, scope, obligations, controls, population, period, evidence, samples, owners, exceptions, incidents, prior findings, and acceptance criteria.
human_authority: Qualified compliance, legal, audit, or domain owners approve criteria, interpretation, samples, findings, reports, exceptions, and attestations. Humans never sign beyond evidence or delegate legal judgment to AI.
ai_boundary: AI may organize criteria, map controls, sample authorized evidence, identify omissions, and draft workpapers. It must preserve source, authority, period, sample, and uncertainty; it must not declare compliance, sign, conceal findings, or communicate externally without human approval.
evidence_requirements: Identify authority, criterion, scope, period, sample, control, source, method, result, reviewer, and limitation. A clean test proves only its criteria, sample, period, and method.
failure_anti_patterns: Checklist compliance, unsupported attestation, stale criteria, sample manipulation, control description as evidence, and AI-generated report treated as qualified assurance.
recovery: Withdraw unsupported result, preserve workpapers, notify authority, remediate, amend report, and reassess deadline or disclosure. Reopen on obligation, scope, period, control, or evidence change.
completion: Authority, criteria, scope, sample, evidence, results, findings, remediation, qualification, limitations, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending qualified acceptance.

title: Safety Testing
purpose: Verify that a system, product, process, or human-AI capability does not create unacceptable hazard under normal, foreseeable misuse, degraded, emergency, maintenance, and recovery conditions.
why_it_matters: Safety depends on interactions among technical behavior, humans, environment, procedures, maintenance, and failure. Simulation, certification, or ordinary operation cannot prove every hazardous condition is controlled.
applies_when: Apply when failure, misuse, automation, environment, or operation can cause injury, illness, unsafe condition, environmental harm, property damage, or loss of critical control.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when qualified safety analysis confirms no hazard or safety-relevant change for the exact scope, population, environment, and lifecycle.
prerequisites: Use safety architecture, hazard analysis, requirements, hardware, software, human factors, operations, maintenance, emergency, legal, and incident baselines. Assign qualified safety authority and stop control.
required_inputs: Hazards, people, environment, modes, controls, assumptions, failure conditions, interfaces, procedures, equipment, data, test limits, emergency response, and acceptance criteria.
human_authority: Qualified safety owners define hazards and limits, authorize testing, stop unsafe work, review evidence, and accept residual risk. Operators and affected people receive clear procedures, training, protection, and reporting paths.
ai_boundary: AI may analyze authorized safety artifacts, enumerate scenarios, draft tests, and identify inconsistencies. It must not infer safety, control hazardous equipment, suppress warnings, approve operation, or substitute simulated confidence for qualified human judgment.
evidence_requirements: Identify hazard, mode, unit, environment, condition, method, observer, time, result, exposure, recovery, and limitation. Certification or simulation proves only its declared standard and scope.
failure_anti_patterns: Testing without safety authority, unsafe setup, alarm ignored, safe state unverified, human error excluded, simulation treated as field proof, and residual hazard hidden as an exception.
recovery: Stop, protect people, enter safe state, preserve evidence, provide emergency response, notify authority, and investigate. Do not resume until qualified review confirms controls and residual risk. Reopen on hazard, mode, environment, population, or design change.
completion: Hazards, people, modes, controls, limits, authority, results, recovery, evidence, residual risk, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending qualified safety acceptance.

title: Model Testing
purpose: Evaluate model behavior, performance, robustness, fairness, calibration, safety, privacy, security, interpretability, and operational drift against its intended use and limits.
why_it_matters: A model can score well overall while failing important populations, contexts, rare events, or safety cases. Test results are sensitive to data, labels, metric choice, threshold, and deployment environment.
applies_when: Apply when a statistical, machine-learning, generative, rules-based, simulation, or decision model influences output, ranking, prediction, classification, recommendation, or action.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability only when no model behavior, data, decision, generated content, or consequential output changes and an approved exact baseline covers the scope.

failure_anti_patterns: Benchmark theater, aggregate-only metrics, leaked test data, self-evaluation, threshold optimized without harm analysis, model drift ignored, and output treated as fact or decision.
recovery: Pause or narrow model use, preserve inputs and outputs, route to human or fallback, notify owners, correct affected decisions, and reassess data and model. Reopen on drift, data, model, provider, policy, population, or harm change.
completion: Purpose, model, data, metrics, slices, limits, human review, evidence, results, recovery, owners, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending independent review and owner acceptance.

why_it_matters: Data can be syntactically valid and still be stale, duplicated, biased, incomplete, misjoined, unauthorized, or semantically wrong. Downstream dashboards or models can amplify a small upstream defect.

does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability when no data meaning, quality, lineage, access, retention, transformation, or consumer behavior changes and an approved exact baseline covers the scope.

failure_anti_patterns: Quality rule without meaning, row count as accuracy, hidden filters, stale data accepted, sensitive samples copied, quarantine bypassed, and corrected data without lineage or consumer notice.
recovery: Quarantine affected data or outputs, preserve versions, notify consumers, correct or backfill, reconcile, restore, and reassess downstream decisions. Reopen on source, schema, definition, transformation, population, or quality change.
completion: Source, grain, meaning, quality, lineage, privacy, owners, tests, corrections, evidence, recovery, limitations, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending independent review and owner acceptance.

title: Test Automation

why_it_matters: Automation increases speed and repeatability but can hide stale tests, weak assertions, data leaks, environment drift, and false confidence. Automation is a tool for evidence, not evidence by itself.

evidence_requirements: Identify test, code version, fixture, runner, environment, dependency, execution, result, artifact, time, actor, and limitation. Automation completion or coverage proves only the recorded execution.
failure_anti_patterns: Brittle automation, retries hiding failures, secrets in logs, test data leakage, assertions too weak, quarantine without owner, and pipeline green while critical tests are skipped.

title: Verification

why_it_matters: Verification answers whether the work conforms to its specification; it does not by itself prove that the specification solves the human problem. Confusing verification with validation creates polished failure.
applies_when: Apply whenever conformance to requirements, design, contract, standard, configuration, or implementation claim matters.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability when no conformance claim is made or an approved exact baseline and lower-risk evidence are sufficient for the scope.

required_inputs: Requirement, source, version, artifact, configuration, method, test, inspection, evidence, result, exception, reviewer, and acceptance criteria.

ai_boundary: AI may trace requirements, inspect authorized artifacts, draft checks, and summarize results. It must not fabricate execution, infer conformance from similarity, alter evidence, or sign verification without human review.
evidence_requirements: Identify requirement, version, artifact, environment, method, execution or inspection, result, reviewer, time, and limitation. A test result proves only the tested requirement and conditions.
failure_anti_patterns: Verification by assertion, stale requirement, untraceable test, conformance inferred from intent, waiver without authority, and verification presented as user validation.

completion: Requirement, artifact, method, evidence, result, deviations, reviewer, conclusion, limitations, and reopening conditions are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE pending independent review and owner acceptance.

why_it_matters: A system can conform perfectly to requirements that were wrong, incomplete, inaccessible, or detached from lived reality. Validation requires evidence from the people and conditions that give the work meaning.
applies_when: Apply when a capability, product, service, policy, model, process, or decision must be shown useful, safe, acceptable, or fit for its intended purpose.

why_it_matters: Configuration is executable behavior. Untracked flags, defaults, environment values, provider settings, and manual changes create drift that can defeat tests, controls, reproducibility, and recovery.
applies_when: Apply when settings, flags, policies, infrastructure, runtime values, schemas, device parameters, or environment-specific behavior can affect an outcome.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability when no configuration or behavior changes and an approved exact baseline covers the artifact and environment.

failure_anti_patterns: Manual production edits, configuration in secrets or source without boundary, undocumented flags, environment drift, default allow, and rollback that restores code but not configuration.
recovery: Freeze drift, preserve state, compare to last valid baseline, roll back or reconcile, rotate exposed values, and reassess impact. Reopen on environment, provider, requirement, dependency, or policy change.

why_it_matters: Incidents require coordinated authority under uncertainty. Unclear command, parallel unsafe action, missing timeline, or premature closure can increase harm and prevent recovery learning.

required_inputs: Alert or report, impact, scope, severity, commander, contacts, evidence, actions, dependencies, communications, recovery objective, and owner authority.

title: System Retirement
purpose: Retire a system completely and responsibly when it no longer serves an approved purpose, replacing or ending it without losing required continuity, evidence, rights, safety, security, or accountability.
why_it_matters: Retirement is more than shutdown. A retired system can leave data, credentials, certificates, DNS, backups, vendors, subscriptions, devices, support promises, undocumented dependencies, and people without a safe path forward. Declaring retirement without proving those boundaries creates hidden liability.
applies_when: Apply whenever a system, product, service, platform, application, process, device fleet, data capability, or organizational technology is permanently removed, replaced, or made unavailable for its prior purpose.
does_not_apply_when: Record non-applicability when no system, service, asset, data, user, dependency, contract, access, operation, or lifecycle state is ending and an approved exact baseline covers the scope. A temporary pause, feature disablement, or environment shutdown is not automatically retirement.
prerequisites: Use lifecycle governance, sunset, deprecation, version, compatibility, migration, data retention, archival, preservation, disposal, deletion, account, service, infrastructure, hardware, legal, financial, security, privacy, support, and continuity baselines. An accountable retirement owner and final approval authority must be named.
required_inputs: Retirement reason, decision authority, scope, dates, owner, users, affected parties, obligations, successor or accepted non-replacement, and acceptable residual risk.

Complete system, service, application, platform, infrastructure, device, data, identity, certificate, DNS, network, vendor, license, subscription, billing, support, backup, archive, and monitoring inventory.
Consumer and dependency map, migration and export requirements, accessibility and support plan, communication, incident and recovery state, legal holds, retention, and disposal rules.
human_authority: The accountable human owner: - states why retirement is necessary and what purpose, population, and scope end; - approves the successor, migration, export, support, communication, timing, risk, and exceptions; - ensures users, operators, customers, suppliers, affected communities, and accountable specialists can raise concerns and obtain recovery or appeal;
ai_boundary: AI may inventory authorized system metadata, discover dependencies, compare successor options, draft migration and communication plans, identify stale access or unresolved artifacts, summarize evidence, and produce a bounded retirement checklist. AI must preserve the difference between intended retirement, planned action, executed action, verified absence, and unresolved uncertainty.
evidence_requirements: Every material claim identifies system and version, environment, owner, scope, source, method, actor, timestamp, result, coverage, and limitation. Evidence may include inventories, dependency queries, access reports, migration reconciliation, export checks, hold checks, vendor certificates, billing closure, DNS and certificate scans, resource absence, hardware custody, user confirmation, and post-shutdown monitoring.

Evidence must distinguish planned, executed, observed, independently verified, stale, partial, contradictory, and unavailable states. “No users found,” “no traffic observed,” “resource deleted,” “invoice closed,” or “script succeeded” proves only the bounded observation.
failure_anti_patterns: Shutdown treated as retirement.
Successor assumed equivalent without validation.
Users, operators, customers, suppliers, or affected communities omitted.
recovery: On unexpected dependency, user harm, active access, traffic, billing, data, evidence, legal hold, safety issue, failed migration, or incomplete cleanup, pause further irreversible action and preserve all remaining state and evidence.

Identify the recovery owner, safe work that may continue, authority required, affected people, evidence needed, and review deadline. Reopen the system or successor path where feasible, restore or extend support, reconcile data, revoke unsafe access, correct public or customer communication, and reassess legal, privacy, financial, safety, environmental, and continuity impact.
completion: Retirement reason, authority, scope, owner, users, successor, dependencies, data, records, access, contracts, finances, support, migration, decommissioning, disposal, evidence, post-shutdown observation, residual risk, unresolved gaps, and final acceptance are explicit. Status remains CONTENT-COMPLETE until independent verification and owner acceptance are separately completed.
source_gaps: Based on the Canonical Section Contract, shared governance requirements, the Owner Cockpit Requirements, the Status and Evidence Lexicon, Sections 001-405, and the section integration roadmap.

The supplied Codex does not provide one universal retirement standard for every jurisdiction, sector, data class, contract, safety regime, environmental material, provider, or system type. Exact legal holds, retention, user rights, successor commitments, recovery windows, disposal methods, supplier obligations, environmental rules, and owner acceptance evidence remain unresolved until supplied for the target system.
learning_objectives: Recognize when the section is materially applicable.
Recognize a near-match where it should not govern.
Assign bounded roles without converting expertise into authority.
Determine what evidence/state is sufficient for the next transition and when to defer/suspend/request evidence.
